title: Single-row space optimization for 0-1 knapsack
summary: Store states in a single one-dimensional array and update capacities in reverse order from high to low so transitions read old values from the previous item's round rather than reusing the same item.
context: There are three items—item 1 apple (weight 1, value 5), item 2 pineapple (weight 2, value 11), and item 3 watermelon (weight 3, value 15)—with maximum knapsack capacity 4, and each item may be chosen at most once. Item IDs i start at 1. The weight and value of item i are stored in wgt[i - 1] and val[i - 1].

The 6 steps demonstrate only the reverse-order update round for outer loop i = 2 (item 2, pineapple). Before this round begins, the one-dimensional array dp[0..4] holds the results [0, 5, 5, 5, 5] for item 1 alone (apple, i = 1); item 3 (watermelon, i = 3) remains unprocessed throughout this figure. Entry dp[c] gives the maximum value within capacity c using items considered so far without requiring the knapsack to be completely full.
description: When processing the pineapple (weight 2, value 11) at capacity c ≥ 2, compare excluding the pineapple (keeping previous-round value dp[c]) with including it (reading previous-round smaller-capacity value dp[c - 2] + 11), writing the larger value back to dp[c]. Traversing capacities c = 4, 3, 2, 1 in reverse order guarantees that dp[c - 2] to the left has not yet been overwritten in this round and still holds its old state from round i = 1 (apple only).

Conversely, updating capacities in forward order from low to high would first update capacity 2 to dp[2] = 11 (already packing one pineapple); evaluating capacity 4 afterward would read dp[2] + 11 = 22, packing the same pineapple twice inside capacity 4 and violating the at-most-once rule of 0-1 knapsack. Reverse-order updates evaluate capacity 4 while dp[2] still holds its old value 5, yielding the correct 5 + 11 = 16.

Each frame shows the 4×5 two-dimensional reference table above and the active single-row array dp[0..4] below. In the single row, blue cells indicate retained old states from the previous round (i = 1) and green cells indicate states already updated in the current round (i = 2); at the end of the round, the entire row turns blue to serve as the old states for processing the watermelon next, with no further numeric changes.

At each step, the single-row table has separate columns for each capacity's value and the round it represents: i = 1 considers only the apple, i = 2 considers the apple and pineapple, and capacity 0 is always boundary 0. Each step also includes the full two-dimensional reference table, where rows for the first 0, first 1, and first 3 items stay unchanged and zeros at capacities 1 to 4 in row 3 remain uncomputed initial values. Both table captions include the step number for direct lookup by step, capacity, and available items.
result: After round 2 (i = 2, pineapple) finishes updating in reverse order, the single-row array is dp = [0, 5, 11, 16, 16], where dp[4] = 16 is only the intermediate maximum value at capacity 4 for the first two items (apple and pineapple); item 3 (watermelon, weight 3, value 15) has not yet been processed, so 16 must not be mistaken for the three-item final answer 20. Derived from the input, choosing the apple and watermelon gives weight 1 + 3 = 4 and value 5 + 15 = 20, which is not drawn in this figure.

frames.title: Begin processing the pineapple
frames.explanation: Before round i = 2 (pineapple, weight 2, value 11) starts, single-row dp[0..4] already holds the valid round i = 1 results [0, 5, 5, 5, 5] (apple only) rather than an all-zero table. Capacity 0 is fixed boundary 0, and capacities 1 through 4 hold old round i = 1 states ready for reverse-order updates starting at maximum capacity c = 4.
frames.key_state: Single-row dp = [0, 5, 5, 5, 5]; capacities 1 through 4 hold old i = 1 states, ready to process the pineapple in reverse from c = 4.

frames.title: Update capacity 4 in reverse order
frames.explanation: Process maximum capacity c = 4 first: excluding the pineapple keeps old value dp[4] = 5; including it reads previous-round old value dp[4 - 2] = dp[2] = 5 (not yet overwritten in this round) plus pineapple value 11 to get 16. Take the larger value to update dp[4] to 16 (round i = 2), while capacities 1, 2, and 3 retain old value 5 from round i = 1. Current single-row dp = [0, 5, 5, 5, 16].
frames.key_state: Entry dp[4] reads old dp[2] = 5 plus 11 to become 16 in round i = 2; capacities 1 to 3 remain 5 from round i = 1; dp = [0, 5, 5, 5, 16].
frames.announcement: Read old value dp[2] = 5 plus 11 to update capacity 4 to 16.

frames.title: Update capacity 3 in reverse order
frames.explanation: Continue in reverse to capacity c = 3: excluding the pineapple keeps old value dp[3] = 5; including it reads old value dp[3 - 2] = dp[1] = 5 from round i = 1 plus 11 to get 16. Update dp[3] to 16 (round i = 2), while capacities 1 and 2 keep old state 5 from round i = 1. Current single-row dp = [0, 5, 5, 16, 16].
frames.key_state: Entry dp[3] reads old dp[1] = 5 plus 11 to become 16; capacities 3 and 4 belong to round i = 2, capacities 1 and 2 remain round i = 1; dp = [0, 5, 5, 16, 16].

frames.title: Update capacity 2 in reverse order
frames.explanation: Continue in reverse to capacity c = 2: excluding the pineapple keeps old value dp[2] = 5; including it reads boundary dp[2 - 2] = dp[0] = 0 plus 11 to get 11. Update dp[2] to 11 (round i = 2). Because reverse order overwrites dp[2] only now, capacity 4 earlier was able to read the unoverwritten old value dp[2] = 5; only capacity 1 still belongs to round i = 1. Current single-row dp = [0, 5, 11, 16, 16].
frames.key_state: Entry dp[2] reads boundary dp[0] = 0 plus 11 to become 11 (i = 2); only capacity 1 remains 5 from round i = 1; dp = [0, 5, 11, 16, 16].
frames.announcement: Read boundary dp[0] = 0 plus 11 to update capacity 2 to 11; only capacity 1 awaits processing.

frames.title: Process capacity 1 where the pineapple does not fit
frames.explanation: Finally process capacity c = 1: because the pineapple weighs 2, exceeding capacity 1, it cannot fit, so the algorithm retains the previous-round value dp[1] = 5. Although dp[1] keeps numeric value 5, capacity 1 has now completed its round 2 (i = 2) check and represents round i = 2 rather than i = 1 (an unchanged number does not mean an unchanged round). Current single-row dp = [0, 5, 11, 16, 16].
frames.key_state: Capacity 1 cannot fit the weight-2 pineapple, keeping value 5 while advancing from round i = 1 to i = 2; all capacities in this round are processed; dp = [0, 5, 11, 16, 16].
frames.announcement: Capacity 1 cannot fit the pineapple, keeping value 5 for round i = 2 and completing round 2.

frames.title: Finish the round and prepare for the next round
frames.explanation: All capacities in round 2 (i = 2, pineapple) have been updated, and single-row dp[0..4] = [0, 5, 11, 16, 16] holds all solutions for the first two items. Performing no new calculation, this frame recolors capacities 1 through 4 from green to blue so the entire row is uniformly blue, indicating these round i = 2 results will serve as the old states when round i = 3 processes item 3 (watermelon), which has not yet started.
frames.key_state: Round 2 complete; dp = [0, 5, 11, 16, 16] becomes the old state for the next round; 16 is only the two-item partial result before processing the watermelon.
frames.announcement: Round 2 complete; single-row [0, 5, 11, 16, 16] becomes the old state for processing the watermelon next.
